newsitem.title: USA: San Diego, QUALCOMM finalize stadium deal.
newsitem.headline: San Diego, QUALCOMM finalize stadium deal.

text.p: The city of San Diego has finalized an $18 million proposal that would rename its stadium after QUALCOMM Inc, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The agreement just has to be executed by both sides," spokesman James Lee said.
The agreement will change the name of San Diego's Jack Murphy Stadium to QUALCOMM Stadium at Jack Murphy Field.
The proposal was approved in concept by the San Diego City Council at a meeting last month. The city council is expected to vote on the final contract next week, Lee said.
Under the terms of the deal, San Diego-based QUALCOMM will pay the city $18 million in cash up-front to have its name on the stadium for the next 20 years.
City officials said San Diego's $78 million stadium expansion project will be financed with $60 million of lease revenue bonds and the $18 million from QUALCOMM.
QUALCOMM develops, manufactures and operates advanced communications systems and products.
